references.text: Names Keturah's sons by Abraham, who are the concubine's sons mentioned in Gen 25:6 as receiving gifts and being sent eastward.
Abraham gave everything he owned to Isaac, which explains why the other sons only received gifts and were sent away.
The expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael is an earlier instance where Abraham sends a son away to protect Isaac's inheritance rights.
Abraham's servant reports that Abraham gave all he had to Isaac, confirming that Isaac was the chosen heir.
God's promise to bless Ishmael and make him into a great nation, relevant because it shows God's plan for Abraham's sons outside the line of Isaac.
1 Chr 1:32-33 lists Keturah's sons, Abraham's concubine, as a parallel to the content in Gen 25:1-6.
